checked_claims.note: The supplied packet hashes to 96775421e0e1440fb7c04fd11e156d83ab93facfaa0ed861bde18398bb5d254e, exactly matching TASK.json and the attempt.
The reviewed target is the exact seven-part C66-GEO-Z theorem_statement from TASK.json, not the global pure-Tate campaign theorem.

Top-degree base change, Fitting minors, relative duality, Riemann-Roch, Serre duality, Clifford, and geometric Riemann-Roch support the intrinsic closed locus and the stated geometric-point equivalences.

Openness of base-point-freeness and balanced splitting on a parameter space of covers does not by itself prove that the image after forgetting the cover is open in Z. The attempt supplies neither a proper/finite presentation of that image nor a direct intrinsic openness argument, especially where h^0(omega(-Gamma)) jumps.

The proof infers nonclosedness from the fact that Z^{bal} is open and nonempty. That implication is invalid. No point of the closure lying outside Z^{bal}, no degeneration to an unbalanced or base-pointed residual pencil, and not even density of the balanced locus is proved; GAP-5 expressly concedes that density is unproved.

The complete-intersection intersection numbers, adjunction, Koszul-Kunneth calculation, and reduced general divisor support nonemptiness of Z. The claimed balanced CE computation is internally derived in the attempt rather than inferred from Tate or motivic predictions.

The Petri-general calculation establishes a smooth 17-dimensional dominant component. It does not determine all components over special curve loci. Thus it does not establish that the whole stack Z has codimension exactly 4 under the standard minimum-codimension convention; the attempt itself records the missing component analysis in GAP-4.

Expected determinantal codimension 6 versus an observed codimension-4 component proves excess dimension relative to the generic determinantal formula. It does not imply that the actual ideal is nowhere locally generated by a regular sequence of length 4. No local commutative-algebra calculation establishing the asserted nowhere-lci conclusion is given.

The quotient-stack torsor statement is correctly kept at stack level, and the attempt does not transfer freeness to coarse moduli. No invariants/coinvariants or cohomological descent assertion is made.

The lemma makes no claim involving integral coefficients, Borel-Moore/cohomology shifts, Poincare twists, Gysin/Kunneth maps, spectral-sequence degeneration, graph automorphisms, semisimplification, motives, or algebraic/tautological generation. Those campaign-level attacks therefore do not repair or refute this exact geometry theorem.

No stable-pair compactification is part of the exact theorem. However, the missing degenerations are precisely what would be needed to justify the theorem's nonclosedness assertion; the proof supplies none.

strongest_attack: Z6 contains an invalid local-algebra inference: expected determinantal codimension 6 together with a codimension-4 dominant component shows excess dimension, but it does not show that Z is nowhere cut out by a regular sequence. Independently, Z3's assertion that the balanced image is not closed is unsupported: nonempty and open does not imply nonclosed, and the attempt explicitly leaves density and boundary degenerations unproved.
theorem_statement: Let k be algebraically closed of characteristic 0, M_{6,6} the moduli stack of smooth proper genus-6 curves with six ordered distinct marked points (smooth DM, dimension 21), pi : C -> M_{6,6} the universal curve with tautological sections sigma_1,...,sigma_6 and universal marking divisor Gamma = sigma_1 + ... + sigma_6, a relative effective Cartier divisor of degree 6 etale over the base, and omega = omega_{C/M}. Define Z := V(Fitt_1(R^1 pi_* O_C(Gamma))) inside M_{6,6}. Then: (Z1) Z is closed, S_6-stable, equals V(Fitt_2(R^1 pi_*(omega(-Gamma)))) and equals V(I_{k-2}(phi)) for every 2-term complex phi : K^0 -> K^1 of vector bundles of ranks k, k-1 universally computing R pi_* O_C(Gamma), and its formation commutes with arbitrary base change. (Z2) A geometric point (C,p_1,...,p_6) lies in Z iff h^0(C,O_C(Gamma)) >= 3, iff h^0(C,omega_C(-Gamma)) >= 2, iff there is a degree-4 line bundle D with h^0(D) >= 2 and Gamma + D in |omega_C|; for C non-hyperelliptic these hold with equality h^0(O_C(Gamma)) = 3 and h^0(omega_C(-Gamma)) = 2, omega_C(-Gamma) is a g^1_4, and they are further equivalent to the six canonical images spanning at most a P^3 in P^5. (Z3) Under the Casnati-Ekedahl normalization O_{P(E^vee)}(1)|_C = omega_C tensor gamma^* O_{P^1}(2) (H1) and the packet balanced splitting F = O_{P^1}(4) + O_{P^1}(5) (H2), for every base-point-free degree-4 morphism gamma : C -> P^1 with tetragonal divisor D_gamma one has W_4|_C = omega_C^{tensor 2} and W_5|_C = omega_C^{tensor 2}(-D_gamma); H^0(C, omega_C tensor W_4^vee(Gamma)) = 0 for every effective degree-6 Gamma; and H^0(C, omega_C tensor W_5^vee(Gamma)) is nonzero iff O_C(Gamma) = W_5 tensor omega_C^{-1} = omega_C(-D_gamma), iff Gamma + D_gamma is canonical. Consequently the image in M_{6,6} of the balanced CE evaluation-failure locus is exactly the OPEN substack Z^{bal} of Z of points at which omega_C(-Gamma) carries a base-point-free pencil with balanced CE splitting; in particular that image is not closed in M_{6,6}, whereas Z is closed and contains it. (Z4) Z is nonempty unconditionally on H1 and H2: a general complete intersection C of divisors of bidegrees (1,2) and (2,2) in P^1 x P^2 is smooth, connected, of genus 6, with omega_C = O_C(1,1), pr_1|_C finite of degree 4, D_gamma = O_C(1,0), and omega_C(-D_gamma) = O_C(0,1) base-point-free of degree 6 with h^0 = 3; a general member of |O_C(0,1)| is reduced with six distinct points and the resulting marked curve lies in Z; for this C the CE data are E^vee = O_{P^1}(-3)^{+3} and F = O_{P^1}(4) + O_{P^1}(5), so Z^{bal} is nonempty as well. (Z5) Z -> M_6 is surjective, and over the Petri-general locus the fibre is the disjoint union over the five points L of W^2_6(C) of the ordered-distinct-support open of |L| = P^2; hence Z has a component dominating M_6, smooth of dimension 17, of codimension 4 in M_{6,6}. (Z6) The determinantal presentation of Z has expected codimension 6 while codim Z = 4, so Z carries excess dimension 2 and is nowhere cut out by a regular sequence in that presentation. (Z7) Z -> [Z/S_6] is a finite etale S_6-torsor of algebraic stacks and [Z/S_6] is canonically the reduced-support open substack of the relative degree-six effective-divisor incidence stack; the corresponding statement on coarse moduli spaces is false because curve automorphisms give nontrivial stabilizers.
